propositions: The DC transport must implement TicketTransport plus SupportsLinks, SupportsComments, and SupportsAbsenceProbe using pycontribs/jira, with the library confined to an optional [jira-datacenter] extra and imported lazily so rebar remains dependency-free.

PAT bearer authentication is read from JIRA_PAT environment variable; JIRA_URL and JIRA_PROJECT come from typed config in [tool.rebar.jira], and malformed config must raise ConfigError rather than degrade to env-only fallback.

Every transport method returns raw payload shapes (e.g., {"key": …, "fields": {…}}) that rebar's existing mappers consume, never leaking jira.Issue objects; transient faults retry with 2s/5s backoff matching acli_rest, HTTP errors never retry, assignee failures raise BackendAssigneeNotFoundError.

TLS validation rejects non-https base_url unless allow_insecure=true is set; certificate verification is never disabled (verify never set to False); ca_bundle configures internal CAs; resolved_statuses customizes the absence probe's resolved-state set, defaulting to {Resolved, Done, Cancelled}.

The NameIdentity resolver's user-search lookup (_search_users_by_username) returns authoritative identity for real users and raises BackendAssigneeNotFoundError for unknown ones, with both unit and live coverage.

All 13 TicketTransport methods (create_issue, get_issue, update_issue, transition_issue_by_name, add_label, search_issues, set_relationship, get_issuelinks_map, map_remote_links, link_payload_for_relation, add_comment, get_comment_map, probe_remote) have passing live tests against the J5 harness that exercise real postconditions on the server and assert through the shared _jira_shape_contract.py contract; self-registration import at adapters/__init__.py line 16 ensures select_backend('jira-datacenter') resolves.
